extracted.intended_audience: prospective Hanna H. Gray Fellows, early-career biomedical researchers, and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: Announcement and summary of the HHMI Hanna H. Gray Fellows program, its goals, selection emphasis, funding terms, and the opening of the next open competition for early-career scientists transitioning from postdoctoral training to independent faculty labs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated commitment to foundational discoveries and inclusive culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows are 'outstanding early career scientists who have demonstrated a commitment to making foundational discoveries while building an inclusive culture in academic science.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection prioritizes candidates who combine high-quality scientific research with active efforts to create an inclusive academic environment. The announcement highlights both discovery and inclusivity as joint expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career stage: postdoctoral through transition to independent lab
rubrics_metrics.description: The program supports fellows 'spanning postdoctoral training through transition to starting their independent lab as a faculty member.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility and program intent focus on early-career investigators at the postdoc-to-faculty transition; the award is structured to accompany candidates through that transition period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research at the forefront / pursuing challenging scientific questions
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI funds fellows who will 'pursue challenging scientific questions at the forefront of their fields.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose work that is ambitious and at the leading edge of their discipline; the program emphasizes intellectual boldness and frontier research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership, mentorship, and ability to recruit and inspire the next generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows are expected to 'recruit, mentor, and inspire the next generation of scientists from all backgrounds' and are described as 'leaders who have proven their dedication to creating a more inclusive future for science.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of mentoring effectiveness, leadership in building lab or departmental culture, and plans to support trainee development and broaden participation are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to building healthy, creative, bold, and effective research environments
rubrics_metrics.description: The HHMI community supports fellows 'where fellows learn with experts and each other how to build healthy research environments that are creative, bold, inclusive, and effective.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate or express commitment to fostering positive research environments; participation in community activities and adopting best practices for lab culture are part of the program's expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for scientists from a broad range of backgrounds and geographies
rubrics_metrics.description: The program 'is committed to supporting scientists from a broad range of backgrounds and geographies.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection processes aim to include diversity across backgrounds and institutional training; the announcement highlights that the 2024 cohort trained at a wide variety of institutions domestically and internationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open competition and nomination policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The competition 'opens immediately' and 'is open to all eligible applicants and no nomination is required.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants do not need an external nomination to apply; the program runs an open submission process. (The announcement points applicants to the program page for details on eligibility and application materials.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection size and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI 'will again select up to 25 fellows' and expects to announce the 2025 competition winners in early 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award cohort size is capped (up to 25 fellows per cycle) and follows a multi-year cadence; applicants should plan around the stated timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Each fellow receives 'up to $1.5 million in support over the span of up to eight years.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding is substantial and multi-year, intended to support trainees from postdoc through establishment of an independent lab; applicants should understand the financial scope and long-duration commitment of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of contributing to HHMI community and professional development
rubrics_metrics.description: New fellows 'join the vibrant, multi-generational HHMI community' to 'learn with experts and each other' regarding research environment building and professional growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond research funding, fellows are expected to engage with HHMI programming, networking, and community efforts that promote inclusive and effective science leadership.
